title: Speed up a routed block-FP8 Mixture-of-Experts layer at 1024 tokens on AMD MI210
summary: This is the routed-expert computation of one Mixture-of-Experts layer on one tensor-parallel rank of a vLLM server on AMD Instinct MI210, for a block-quantized FP8 model with BF16 activations. The implementation in moe_w8a16.py and its two tile tables is what the server runs today, and it is correct. You must make the whole layer call faster (token sort, the two expert matmuls, SiLU-and-mul and the top-k sum) for one batch size, 1024 tokens, with routing drawn from expert counts recorded on a real server. Inputs are the hidden states, the FP8 weights with their block scales, and the top-k expert ids and weights; the output is this rank's partial sum. Metric: continuous performance score on that one batch size after a hard correctness gate over all batch sizes (error within 1.02x of the baseline's, deterministic, no compilation during inference), on a logarithmic curve relative to the oracle anchor, calibrated on MI210, not comparable with H20 anchors.
runner_docstring:
Frozen runner (do NOT modify): python3 scripts/task_runner.py compile | correctness | performance

One routed-expert MoE layer on one TP rank of MI210: 100 experts, all local, top-8, hidden 2560, expert intermediate 384 per rank, block-FP8 (128x128) e4m3fn weights, BF16 activations. baseline_* is the frozen baseline: every correctness tolerance is anchored to it. See /app/instruction.md for the rules.

negative.replace: accumulator = accumulator * 1.0  # router weight dropped: must fail correctness
negative.why: Drops the router weight on the served down GEMM path (rows m1 and m512 up), which changes the result.
